title: runtime-inference-api-surface-draft-v1
content:
Summary: Draft of the runtime-facing inference API surface. This doc focuses on request/response schemas, structured error codes, compatibility guarantees across hosted/dedicated/private, and runtime-level hints (scheduling, kernel selection, KV cache controls). Purpose: provide a concrete starting point for SDKs, gateway routing, and runtime implementers. Not final — lots of open questions called out.

Goals and constraints:
- Minimal, backwards-compatible baseline for text generation + chat + kv ops.
- Explicit fields for runtime hints (scheduling_priority, kernel_hint, cache_policy) but optional so older clients continue to work.
- Strong idempotency and retry semantics for transient failures.
- Clear deprecation and compatibility policy to allow kernel/runtime evolution without breaking customer workloads.

Terminology:
- request_id: client-supplied opaque id for tracing (UUID recommended).
- model_variant: canonical model id + variant tag (e.g., gptx-4-8k:q4_0).
- runtime_hint: guidance to the serving layer; treated as hint, not contract.

Top-level endpoints (conceptual):
- POST /v1/runtime/generate -> single-shot generation (sync + streaming)
- POST /v1/runtime/chat -> conversation-style (history + delta streaming)
- POST /v1/runtime/kv-checkpoint -> KV cache management (pin/unpin/inspect)
- GET /v1/runtime/models/:model_variant/compat -> compatibility metadata for a variant

Request schema (JSON) — generate (flattened):
- request_id: string (optional, recommended)
- client: { name: string, version: string } (optional, simple map — SDKs should populate)
- model: string (required) // e.g., "rw-2l-large:1" or a catalog id
- prompt: string | [string | object] // single string or mixed content blocks (deprecated in short-term)
- max_tokens: integer (optional)
- temperature: float (optional)
- top_p: float (optional)
- stop: [string] (optional)
- streaming: boolean (optional; default=false)
- idempotency_key: string (optional) — used to dedupe retried requests for side-effect-free generation
- runtime_hints: { scheduling_priority?: string, kernel_hint?: string, cache_policy?: string } (optional)
- cache_key: string (optional) — explicit key to read/write KV cache; mutually exclusive with cache_policy="no-cache"

Notes: runtime_hints are advisory only. scheduling_priority may be one of [low, normal, high, urgent]. kernel_hint may be a family tag like "flash-attn-v2", "quantized-int8". cache_policy may be ["no-cache", "read-only", "write-if-miss", "force-refresh"].

Response schema (success):
- request_id: string (echoed)
- model: string (resolved model id)
- variant: string (runtime-picked variant)
- tokens: [ { index: integer, text: string, logprob?: float } ] OR streaming chunk frames
- usage: { input_tokens: integer, output_tokens: integer, cpu_ms?: integer, gpu_ms?: integer }
- cache_result: { hit: boolean, key?: string, size_bytes?: integer } (optional)
- warnings: [string] (optional)

Errors: high-level shape:
- code: string (machine-readable)
- status: integer (HTTP mapping)
- message: string (human readable)
- details: [string] (optional)
- transient: boolean (optional hint for retry)
- retry_after_seconds: integer (optional)
- request_id: string (echoed if present)

Proposed error code taxonomy (string codes):
- invalid_request.parameters_missing (400) — client-side schema problems
- invalid_model.unknown (404) — model id not found in catalog
- invalid_model.incompatible_variant (409) — requested spec incompatible with model variant (e.g., requested int8 with a model-only available as fp16)
- runtime.resource_exhausted (429) — caps reached, includes details about fallback suggestions
- runtime.kernel_failure (500) — kernel crash / internal compute error; transient=true
- runtime.kv_corruption (500) — KV cache store issues; transient may be false depending on root cause
- runtime.incompatible_semantics (412) — client requested a semantic contract (e.g., strict deterministic_seeding) not supported
- auth.missing_or_invalid (401)
- rate.limit_exceeded (429)
- deprecated.endpoint_used (410) — optional header deprecation meta included

Compatibility guarantees (draft):
- Backward compatibility (high priority):
  - New optional request fields (runtime_hints, cache_key) must not change request outcome for older runtimes. Older runtimes should ignore unknown fields.
  - Responses may add top-level fields; SDKs should access by key and not assume fixed ordering.
- Forward compatibility (best-effort):
  - Runtimes should reject requests that contain explicit fields they cannot safely handle with a 412 + runtime.incompatible_semantics. Example: client sets "deterministic_seed" but model variant cannot support deterministic behavior.
- Model variant compatibility:
  - Each model variant has a compatibility manifest accessible via GET /models/:variant/compat that lists supported request subfeatures (streaming, kv_cache, token_timestamps). SDKs should query this once per session and cache results.
- Deprecation policy:
  - Soft deprecation: feature marked as deprecated in compat manifest and returns a deprecated.endpoint_used warning. Soft-deprecated fields continue to work for 90 days.
  - Hard deprecation: after 90 days, server may return 410 for the field if present. Major breaking changes require 180-day notice via console + API header, and a migration guide.

KV cache behavior and API notes:
- KV cache is per-customer per-model_variant logical store. Keys are opaque strings owned by the client but must include enough entropy to avoid collisions.
- Write semantics: by default, write-if-miss when cache_policy is unset. If cache_policy==force-refresh the runtime overwrites existing entry. read-only never writes.
- Durability: hosted runtime: soft persistence with replication across nodes. Dedicated/Private: behavior documented in private-deployments/KV-SLA.md (TODO link).
- Atomicity: single request may produce multiple KV writes during generation (prefix caching). The runtime will attempt best-effort atomic upsert per-key, but cross-key atomicity is not guaranteed.
- KV consistency modes (configurable at deployment):
  - eventual (default): best throughput, lower latency; gets weaker guarantees on cross-node reads.
  - strong (opt-in on dedicated/private): linearizable reads/writes; may increase latency.

Scheduling and kernel selection hints (runtime_hint semantics):
- scheduling_priority: affects queue ordering and preemption preferences. Only absolute 'urgent' may preempt normal workloads but subject to quota.
- kernel_hint: runtime will use as a soft preference. If unavailable, runtime falls back to compatible kernel and returns a warning with suggested variant to avoid.
- kernel selection is ultimately the runtime's decision; kernels may be swapped mid-request only for non-streaming ops. Streaming requests cannot change kernel after first chunk without restarting stream.

Idempotency and retries:
- idempotency_key dedup window: 5 minutes for generation requests unless overridden by per-customer policy.
- Retry strategy: clients may retry on transient=true with exponential backoff. Retry-after is authoritative if provided.
- Side-effects: generation is treated as side-effect-free by default. If request triggers billing-related state (rare), server will return non-idempotent error and must document required flow.

Streaming semantics (notes):
- Server-sent events (SSE) or chunked HTTP used for streaming. Each chunk contains request_id, sequence index, text delta, and optional kernel_metrics.
- Resuming a stream: clients may reconnect with last_received_token_index to resume in-flight streams only if model variant supports stream checkpoints (listed in compat manifest).

Versioning and header conventions:
- API root includes version: /v1/runtime/...
- Semantic fields changes use minor version bumps for additive, major for breaking. We favor additive changes.
- Response headers to include: X-Request-ID (echo), X-Model-Variant-Hash (short id), Deprecation-Warn (header with ISO date)

Telemetry and SDK guidance:
- SDKs should surface structured error.code and transient flag for automatic retry plugins.
- SDKs should perform a single compat manifest fetch per app session and cache results for 24h.
- Console will surface model/variant incompatibilities discovered in logs as opt-in alerts to customers.

Open questions / action items:
- [ACTION] Decide exact idempotency dedupe window (5 minutes provisional) — ENG-1293
- [QUESTION] Should cache_key be namespaced by customer id server-side or require client to prefix? (security + multi-tenant collision concern)
- [ACTION] Wire up dedicated/private KV durability docs and link from this doc (TODO)
- [DISCUSS] How to represent multi-block prompt structured inputs in a long-term stable schema without breaking older SDKs?
- [TODO] Align error codes with platform-wide error catalog (SRE / Platform API) — contact Samir Kapoor

Examples (concise)
1) Simple generate request:
POST /v1/runtime/generate
{
  "request_id": "c9d8f8e2-4a2b-4f3b-b0a1-9c3f7e1a2b22",
  "client": { "name": "rw-js", "version": "1.2.0" },
  "model": "rw-2l-large:1",
  "prompt": "Write a concise explanation of KV cache semantics.",
  "max_tokens": 180,
  "temperature": 0.0,
  "runtime_hints": { "scheduling_priority": "high", "kernel_hint": "quant-int8" },
  "cache_key": "user-123-session-456-prefix-v1"
}

2) Error example (kernel failure):
HTTP/1.1 500
{
  "code": "runtime.kernel_failure",
  "status": 500,
  "message": "GPU kernel crashed during matmul. Fallback to fp16 attempted and succeeded.",
  "details": ["kernel=matmul_v3"],
  "transient": true,
  "request_id": "c9d8f8e2-4a2b-4f3b-b0a1-9c3f7e1a2b22"
}

Notes to reviewers:
- Please review the error taxonomy and call out missing cases (esp around KV durability and auth errors).
- Keep comments inline in the PR (linked in linked_artifacts) or ping on #eng-serving-runtime.

Rough revision history:
- v0.1 (2026-02-20) initial draft with basic schema
- v0.2 (2026-03-11) added KV semantics, streaming resume note, error taxonomy expansion
